{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /logs/agent/sessions/skills/python-scala-functional\n\n# Python to Scala Functional Programming Translation\n\n\n## Numeric Formatting\n\nUse this translation when Python code formats floating-point or decimal values with fixed precision.\nThis Scala version preserves the same intent: rounding to the specified number of decimal places and returning a plain decimal string without scientific notation.\n\nPython:\n\n```python\nf\"{value:.{precision}f}\"\n```\n\nScala:\n```scala\nval strValue =\n  BigDecimal.decimal(value)\n    .setScale(precision, BigDecimal.RoundingMode.HALF_UP)\n    .bigDecimal\n    .toPlainString\n```\n\n\n## Higher-Order Functions\n\n```python\n# Python\ndef apply_twice(f, x):\n    return f(f(x))\n\ndef make_multiplier(n):\n    return lambda x: x * n\n\ndouble = make_multiplier(2)\nresult = apply_twice(double, 5)  # 20\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala\ndef applyTwice[A](f: A => A, x: A): A = f(f(x))\n\ndef makeMultiplier(n: Int): Int => Int = x => x * n\n\nval double = makeMultiplier(2)\nval result = applyTwice(double, 5)  // 20\n```\n\n## Decorators → Function Composition\n\n```python\n# Python\ndef log_calls(func):\n    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):\n        print(f\"Calling {func.__name__}\")\n        result = func(*args, **kwargs)\n        print(f\"Finished {func.__name__}\")\n        return result\n    return wrapper\n\n@log_calls\ndef add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - function composition\ndef logCalls[A, B](f: A => B, name: String): A => B = { a =>\n  println(s\"Calling $name\")\n  val result = f(a)\n  println(s\"Finished $name\")\n  result\n}\n\nval add = (a: Int, b: Int) => a + b\nval loggedAdd = logCalls(add.tupled, \"add\")\n\n// Alternative: using by-name parameters\ndef withLogging[A](name: String)(block: => A): A = {\n  println(s\"Calling $name\")\n  val result = block\n  println(s\"Finished $name\")\n  result\n}\n```\n\n## Pattern Matching\n\n```python\n# Python (3.10+)\ndef describe(value):\n    match value:\n        case 0:\n            return \"zero\"\n        case int(x) if x > 0:\n            return \"positive int\"\n        case int(x):\n            return \"negative int\"\n        case [x, y]:\n            return f\"pair: {x}, {y}\"\n        case {\"name\": name, \"age\": age}:\n            return f\"{name} is {age}\"\n        case _:\n            return \"unknown\"\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - pattern matching is more powerful\ndef describe(value: Any): String = value match {\n  case 0 => \"zero\"\n  case x: Int if x > 0 => \"positive int\"\n  case _: Int => \"negative int\"\n  case (x, y) => s\"pair: $x, $y\"\n  case List(x, y) => s\"list of two: $x, $y\"\n  case m: Map[_, _] if m.contains(\"name\") =>\n    s\"${m(\"name\")} is ${m(\"age\")}\"\n  case _ => \"unknown\"\n}\n\n// Case class pattern matching (preferred)\nsealed trait Result\ncase class Success(value: Int) extends Result\ncase class Error(message: String) extends Result\n\ndef handle(result: Result): String = result match {\n  case Success(v) if v > 100 => s\"Big success: $v\"\n  case Success(v) => s\"Success: $v\"\n  case Error(msg) => s\"Failed: $msg\"\n}\n```\n\n## Option Handling (None/null Safety)\n\n```python\n# Python\ndef find_user(user_id: int) -> Optional[User]:\n    user = db.get(user_id)\n    return user if user else None\n\ndef get_user_email(user_id: int) -> Optional[str]:\n    user = find_user(user_id)\n    if user is None:\n        return None\n    return user.email\n\n# Chained operations\ndef get_user_city(user_id: int) -> Optional[str]:\n    user = find_user(user_id)\n    if user is None:\n        return None\n    address = user.address\n    if address is None:\n        return None\n    return address.city\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - Option monad\ndef findUser(userId: Int): Option[User] = db.get(userId)\n\ndef getUserEmail(userId: Int): Option[String] =\n  findUser(userId).map(_.email)\n\n// Chained operations with flatMap\ndef getUserCity(userId: Int): Option[String] =\n  findUser(userId)\n    .flatMap(_.address)\n    .map(_.city)\n\n// For-comprehension (cleaner for multiple operations)\ndef getUserCity(userId: Int): Option[String] = for {\n  user <- findUser(userId)\n  address <- user.address\n  city <- Option(address.city)\n} yield city\n\n// Getting values out\nval email = getUserEmail(1).getOrElse(\"no-email@example.com\")\nval emailOrThrow = getUserEmail(1).get  // Throws if None\n```\n\n## Generators → Iterators/LazyList\n\n```python\n# Python\ndef fibonacci():\n    a, b = 0, 1\n    while True:\n        yield a\n        a, b = b, a + b\n\n# Take first 10\nfibs = list(itertools.islice(fibonacci(), 10))\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - LazyList (was Stream in Scala 2.12)\ndef fibonacci: LazyList[BigInt] = {\n  def loop(a: BigInt, b: BigInt): LazyList[BigInt] =\n    a #:: loop(b, a + b)\n  loop(0, 1)\n}\n\nval fibs = fibonacci.take(10).toList\n\n// Alternative: Iterator\ndef fibonacciIterator: Iterator[BigInt] = new Iterator[BigInt] {\n  private var (a, b) = (BigInt(0), BigInt(1))\n  def hasNext: Boolean = true\n  def next(): BigInt = {\n    val result = a\n    val newB = a + b\n    a = b\n    b = newB\n    result\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Try/Either for Error Handling\n\n```python\n# Python - exceptions\ndef parse_int(s: str) -> int:\n    try:\n        return int(s)\n    except ValueError:\n        return 0\n\n# Python - Optional for errors\ndef safe_parse_int(s: str) -> Optional[int]:\n    try:\n        return int(s)\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - Try monad\nimport scala.util.{Try, Success, Failure}\n\ndef parseInt(s: String): Try[Int] = Try(s.toInt)\n\nval result = parseInt(\"123\") match {\n  case Success(n) => s\"Got: $n\"\n  case Failure(e) => s\"Error: ${e.getMessage}\"\n}\n\n// Chaining Try operations\nval doubled = parseInt(\"123\").map(_ * 2)\n\n// Either for custom error types\ndef parsePositive(s: String): Either[String, Int] = {\n  Try(s.toInt).toEither\n    .left.map(_ => \"Not a number\")\n    .flatMap { n =>\n      if (n > 0) Right(n)\n      else Left(\"Must be positive\")\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Function Composition\n\n```python\n# Python\ndef compose(f, g):\n    return lambda x: f(g(x))\n\ndef pipe(*functions):\n    def inner(x):\n        result = x\n        for f in functions:\n            result = f(result)\n        return result\n    return inner\n\n# Usage\nadd_one = lambda x: x + 1\ndouble = lambda x: x * 2\npipeline = pipe(add_one, double, add_one)  # (x + 1) * 2 + 1\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - built-in composition\nval addOne: Int => Int = _ + 1\nval double: Int => Int = _ * 2\n\n// compose: f.compose(g) = f(g(x))\nval composed = addOne.compose(double)  // addOne(double(x))\n\n// andThen: f.andThen(g) = g(f(x))\nval pipeline = addOne.andThen(double).andThen(addOne)  // (x + 1) * 2 + 1\n```\n\n## Currying and Partial Application\n\n```python\n# Python\nfrom functools import partial\n\ndef add(a, b, c):\n    return a + b + c\n\nadd_5 = partial(add, 5)\nresult = add_5(3, 2)  # 10\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - curried functions\ndef add(a: Int)(b: Int)(c: Int): Int = a + b + c\n\nval add5 = add(5) _  // Partially applied\nval result = add5(3)(2)  // 10\n\n// Converting between curried and uncurried\nval uncurried = Function.uncurried(add _)\nval curried = (uncurried _).curried\n\n// Multiple parameter lists\ndef fold[A, B](init: B)(list: List[A])(f: (B, A) => B): B =\n  list.foldLeft(init)(f)\n\nval sum = fold(0)(List(1, 2, 3))(_ + _)\n```\n\n## Tail Recursion\n\n```python\n# Python - no tail call optimization\ndef factorial(n):\n    if n <= 1:\n        return 1\n    return n * factorial(n - 1)\n\n# Workaround: iterative\ndef factorial_iter(n):\n    result = 1\n    for i in range(2, n + 1):\n        result *= i\n    return result\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - tail recursion with annotation\nimport scala.annotation.tailrec\n\ndef factorial(n: Int): BigInt = {\n  @tailrec\n  def loop(n: Int, acc: BigInt): BigInt = {\n    if (n <= 1) acc\n    else loop(n - 1, n * acc)\n  }\n  loop(n, 1)\n}\n```\n\n## Implicit Conversions and Type Classes\n\n```python\n# Python - no direct equivalent\n# Duck typing provides flexibility\n```\n\n```scala\n// Scala - type classes via implicits (Scala 2) or given/using (Scala 3)\n\n// Scala 3\ntrait Show[A]:\n  def show(a: A): String\n\ngiven Show[Int] with\n  def show(a: Int): String = s\"Int: $a\"\n\ndef display[A](a: A)(using s: Show[A]): String = s.show(a)\n\n// Scala 2\ntrait Show[A] {\n  def show(a: A): String\n}\n\nimplicit val intShow: Show[Int] = new Show[Int] {\n  def show(a: Int): String = s\"Int: $a\"\n}\n\ndef display[A](a: A)(implicit s: Show[A]): String = s.show(a)\n```\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"643562c5-6642-4a08-99e6-e929d464f1d5","uuid":"562d43cf-5478-42f7-bcfb-e0696377a7ca","timestamp":"2026-03-27T02:52:42.796Z","isSynthetic":true}

Map(\"original_type\" -> \"Int\"))\n\n  def tokenizeBigDecimal(value: BigDecimal): Token = {\n    val str = value\n      .setScale(precision, BigDecimal.RoundingMode.HALF_UP)\n      .bigDecimal\n      .toPlainString\n    Token(str, TokenType.NUMERIC, Map(\"original_type\" -> \"BigDecimal\"))\n  }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// TemporalTokenizer\n// ============================================================================\n\nclass TemporalTokenizer(formatStr: Option[String] = None)\n    extends BaseTokenizer[LocalDateTime] {\n\n  private val defaultDateTimeFormat: DateTimeFormatter =\n    DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(\"yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss\")\n  private val defaultDateFormat: DateTimeFormatter =\n    DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(\"yyyy-MM-dd\")\n\n  def tokenize(value: LocalDateTime): Token = {\n    val fmt = formatStr.fold(defaultDateTimeFormat)(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern)\n    Token(value.format(fmt), TokenType.TEMPORAL)\n  }\n\n  def tokenizeDate(value: LocalDate): Token = {\n    val fmt = formatStr.fold(defaultDateFormat)(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern)\n    Token(value.format(fmt), TokenType.TEMPORAL)\n  }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// UniversalTokenizer  (runtime dispatch via overloading)\n// ============================================================================\n\nclass UniversalTokenizer {\n  private val stringTokenizer   = new StringTokenizer()\n  private val numericTokenizer  = new NumericTokenizer()\n  private val temporalTokenizer = new TemporalTokenizer()\n\n  def tokenizeNull: Token                   = Token(\"NULL\", TokenType.NULL)\n  def tokenize(value: String): Token        = stringTokenizer.tokenize(value)\n  def tokenize(value: Array[Byte]): Token   = stringTokenizer.tokenizeBytes(value)\n  def tokenize(value: Int): Token           = numericTokenizer.tokenizeInt(value)\n  def tokenize(value: Double): Token        = numericTokenizer.tokenize(value)\n  def tokenize(value: BigDecimal): Token    = numericTokenizer.tokenizeBigDecimal(value)\n  def tokenize(value: LocalDateTime): Token = temporalTokenizer.tokenize(value)\n  def tokenize(value: LocalDate): Token     = temporalTokenizer.tokenizeDate(value)\n  def tokenize(value: Tokenizable): Token   = Token(value.toToken, TokenType.STRUCTURED)\n\n  /** Fallback for unsupported types — delegates to toString. */\n  def tokenizeAny(value: Any): Token =\n    Token(value.toString, TokenType.STRING, Map(\"fallback\" -> true))\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// TokenRegistry\n// ============================================================================\n\nclass TokenRegistry[T] {\n  private var registry: Map[String, TokenContainer[T]] = Map.empty\n  private var handlers: List[T => Option[Token]]       = Nil\n\n  def register(key: String, container: TokenContainer[T]): Unit =\n    registry = registry.updated(key, container)\n\n  def addHandler(handler: T => Option[Token]): Unit =\n    handlers = handlers :+ handler\n\n  /** For each item in the named container, tries handlers in registration\n   *  order and returns the first successful result, or None if no handler\n   *  matched.\n   */\n  def process(key: String): List[Option[Token]] =\n    registry.get(key).fold(List.empty[Option[Token]]) { container =>\n      container.getAll.toList.map { item =>\n        handlers.iterator.flatMap(h => h(item)).nextOption()\n      }\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// TokenFunctor / TokenMonad\n// ============================================================================\n\nclass TokenFunctor[T](private val _value: T) {\n  def get: T = _value\n\n  def map[B](f: T => B): TokenFunctor[B]                    = new TokenFunctor(f(_value))\n  def flatMap[B](f: T => TokenFunctor[B]): {\n  override def map[B](f: T => B): TokenMonad[B] = new TokenMonad(f(get))\n\n  /** Applicative apply — unwrap the function inside funcWrapped and apply it. */\n  def ap[B](funcWrapped: TokenMonad[T => B]): TokenMonad[B] =\n    new TokenMonad(funcWrapped.get(get))\n}\n\nobject TokenMonad {\n  def pure[T](value: T): TokenMonad[T] = new TokenMonad(value)\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// JsonTokenizer  (uses Circe)\n// ============================================================================\n\nclass JsonTokenizer(pretty: Boolean = false) {\n\n  def tokenize(value: Json): Token = {\n    val jsonStr = if (pretty) value.spaces2 else value.noSpaces\n    Token(jsonStr, TokenType.STRUCTURED, Map(\"json\" -> true))\n  }\n\n  /** Navigate a dot-delimited path inside a JSON value and tokenize the leaf. */\n  def tokenizePath(value: Json, path: String): Option[Token] = {\n    val parts = path.split('.')\n    val resolved = parts.foldLeft(Option(value)) { (current, part) =>\n      current.flatMap { json =>\n        json.asObject.flatMap(_.apply(part))\n          .orElse(\n            json.asArray.flatMap { arr =>\n              Try(part.toInt).toOption.flatMap(arr.lift)\n            }\n          )\n      }\n    }\n    resolved.map(tokenize)\n  }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// WhitespaceTokenizer\n// ============================================================================\n\nclass WhitespaceTokenizer(\n  lowercase:        Boolean        = false,\n  minLength:        Int            = 0,\n  maxLength:        Option[Int]    = None,\n  stripPunctuation: Boolean        = false\n) {\n  private val punctuationChars: Set[Char] = \".,!?;:'\\\"()[]{}\".toSet\n\n  private def processToken(word: String): Option[String] = {\n    val stripped =\n      if (stripPunctuation)\n        word\n          .dropWhile(c => punctuationChars.contains(c))\n          .reverse\n          .dropWhile(c => punctuationChars.contains(c))\n          .reverse\n      else word\n\n    val cased     = if (lowercase) stripped.toLowerCase else stripped\n    val truncated = maxLength.fold(cased)(cased.take)\n\n    if (truncated.length < minLength || truncated.isEmpty) None\n    else Some(truncated)\n  }\n\n  def tokenize(text: String): List[Token] =\n    text.split(\"\\\\s+\").toList.zipWithIndex.flatMap { case (word, idx) =>\n      processToken(word).map { processed =>\n        Token(processed, tokenizeWithPositions(text: String): List[(String, Int, Int)] = {\n    var pos = 0\n    text.split(\"\\\\s+\").toList.flatMap { word =>\n      val start = text.indexOf(word, pos)\n      val end   = start + word.length\n      pos = end\n      processToken(word).map(processed => (processed, start, end))\n    }\n  }\n\n  def countTokens(text: String): Int = tokenize(text).size\n}\n\n// the builder itself is\n *  thread-safe and composable without accidental mutation.\n */\nfinal class TokenizerBuilder[T] private (\n  normalizers: List[String => String],\n  validators:  List[T => Boolean],\n  metadataMap: Map[String, Any]\n) {\n\n  def withNormalizer(f: String => String): TokenizerBuilder[T] =\n    new TokenizerBuilder(normalizers :+ f, validators, metadataMap)\n\n  def withValidator(f: T => Boolean): TokenizerBuilder[T] =\n    new TokenizerBuilder(normalizers, validators :+ f, metadataMap)\n\n  def withMetadata(pairs: (String, Any)*): TokenizerBuilder[T] =\n    new TokenizerBuilder(normalizers, validators, metadataMap ++ pairs)\n\n  def build(): T => Token = { value =>\n    validators.find(v => !v(value)).foreach { _ =>\n      throw new IllegalArgumentException(s\"Validation failed for $value\")\n    }\n    val normalized = normalizers.foldLeft(value.toString)((s, f) => f(s))\n    Token(normalized, TokenType.STRING, metadataMap)\n
